boundary: This is the canonical overall inventory for capability status, dependency order, and assignment. It separates durable product capabilities from operator-owned external evidence, human decisions, and optional optimization; release-readiness authorities remain the delegated validators for their evidence gates. Local or fixture proof can complete a code capability, but it cannot promote hosted, release, or production evidence.
status_boundary: Capability status is a reviewed source-control judgment. Validation checks dependency shape, source anchors, release authority, and package commands without executing proofs or treating ignored target artifacts as fresh evidence.

items.title: Event store and replayable projections
items.summary: Append-only Postgres streams, optimistic concurrency, synchronous projections, and deterministic rebuild audits form the durable state boundary.
complete_when: Committed events rebuild every declared projection without drift.

items.title: Deterministic resolution engine and pack parity
items.summary: The closed rules IR and deterministic resolver cover the full source-derived engine inventory; this is local engine parity, not hosted product readiness.
complete_when: Every actionable in-scope engine inventory row is supported and validated, and every remaining unsupported row is explicitly classified out of scope.

items.title: Capability-gated command runtime
items.summary: Typed commands resolve authority at the boundary, append events transactionally, update projections, and return idempotent acknowledgements.
complete_when: Commands preserve capability, concurrency, idempotency, and event-log invariants through the Postgres pipeline.

items.title: Versioned wire and recoverable live delivery
items.summary: Versioned Rust-owned wire types, REST/JSON commands and cold loads, binary-CBOR WebSocket projection delivery, lag resync, and frontend hydration recovery are locally proven.
complete_when: A seeded client can cold-load, decode only versioned binary-CBOR live frames, recover from lag, and retain capability-filtered state.

items.title: Host setup workbench
items.summary: The host setup role URL drives roster, role, policy, start-phase, stale-command rejection, and recovery through the real command path.
complete_when: A seeded host can configure and start a valid game from the setup role URL and recover from a stale mutation.

items.title: Multi-replica release topology
items.summary: The API now uses shared async object media, migration-free startup, an explicit pre-deploy migrator, and a locally proven two-instance media/live recovery boundary.
complete_when: API startup is migration-free, an explicit migrator owns schema changes, shared S3-compatible media preserves the existing content-addressed contract, and a two-replica local or hosted proof exercises cross-replica media and live recovery.
items.boundary: The local proof drives two API instances against one Postgres pool and one shared object repository: instance A uploads and commands, instance B serves the committed variant, observes the live change, and rehydrates on reconnect. The Railway source contract requires a pre-deploy migrator and two API replicas. This closes the code capability, not hosted race evidence, production promotion, or release readiness.

items.title: 1.0 security release baseline
items.summary: The production frontend uses a browser-proven nonce CSP, release secrets have an environment-isolated custody and rotation contract, deployable images have locked provenance, and source plus artifact proofs reject sensitive telemetry.
complete_when: A strict production CSP, secret custody/rotation configuration, dependency/container provenance checks, and no-sensitive-telemetry contracts are enforced and locally proven.
items.boundary: This closes the source-controlled and local-browser security release baseline. The SvelteKit accessibility announcer is the sole inline-style exception and is authorized by an exact CSP hash; executable inline content remains nonce-bound. Secret evidence contains policy and version markers only, never values. Third-party penetration testing, compliance certification, hosted telemetry retention, incident response rehearsal, and production promotion remain independent release evidence.

items.title: Reviewable 1.0 core and toolchain
items.summary: Rust 1.95.0 and strict workspace Clippy are proof-enforced; API media, auth, community, game-read HTTP, live WebSocket delivery, authentication attempt/delivery, and live publication, domain pack model/validation, resolver action/trigger/outcome, and projection effect/private-channel ownership are isolated behind typed boundaries. Remaining resolver coordinator, API command/import transport, other projection, command-test, and proof-runner concentrations remain inventoried.
complete_when: The Rust toolchain is pinned, workspace Clippy is warning-clean, and concentrated pack, resolver, API, projection, command-test, and proof orchestration responsibilities are split into coherent modules without weakening proof coverage.
remaining: Split remaining resolver coordinator, API command/import transport, other projection, command-test, and proof-runner responsibilities along the dependency direction recorded in docs/arch/16-maintainable-core.md.
Remove the exact lint expectations as typed contexts and bounded modules supersede them.

recommended_slice.objective: Extract command submission/preparation and completed-game import from crates/api/src/lib.rs into a typed command HTTP owner: move /commands and /games/import routes, wire command adaptation, media-reference preparation, idempotent dispatch, live-publication dirty-surface classification handoff, and import authorization behind a bounded state; keep router composition, auth/game/community/media/live-delivery route families, and live change publication in their current owners; preserve protocol version, reject mapping, idempotency, and projection publish semantics.
non_claims: Do not move command decisioning into the HTTP boundary; keep commands::handle_idempotent as the write owner.
Do not merge live delivery or live publication into the command HTTP owner.
Do not change command URLs, wire DTOs, reject codes, or publish dirty-surface classification as an accidental side effect of extraction.
Do not mark foundation.maintainable-core complete; remaining resolver coordinator, other projection families, command-test, and proof-runner concentrations remain.

items.title: Seeded playable core loop
items.summary: Seeded host and player role URLs exercise posting, voting, actions, phase resolution, stale recovery, and completion in a real local game.
complete_when: The core live spine completes through browser role surfaces with its saved proof contract green.

items.title: Host and cohost moderation controls
items.summary: Host and delegated cohost controls cover deadlines, phases, prompts, publication, lifecycle changes, completion, conflict rejection, and reload recovery.
complete_when: Every shipped critical moderation control has a typed command, projection result, rejection boundary, and seeded role-surface proof.

items.title: Replacement continuity and authority transfer
items.summary: Replacement preserves slot history while transferring role URLs, sessions, actions, votes, and private-channel authority with stale outgoing denial.
complete_when: Incoming authority recovers across reconnect/reload and outgoing credentials cannot retain current slot capabilities.

items.title: Reveal-gated endgame and vote history
items.summary: Completed games reveal roles and resolved vote history only after completion and preserve them through stale recovery, resync, and reload.
complete_when: Normal and stale player surfaces converge on the same reveal-gated endgame summary and durable vote history.

items.title: Typed DayEvent and reward model
items.summary: A database-free platform model owns validated DayEvent identity, lifecycle, schedules, participation, deterministic resolution evidence, narratives, reward bindings, and concrete effect plans without duplicating the rules engine.
complete_when: Invalid DayEvent states fail closed and valid schedules, decisions, narratives, rewards, and terminal transitions are deterministic values.

items.title: Immutable DayProgram library
items.summary: Hosts select product-visible, versioned, BLAKE3-pinned DayPrograms through a checked-in catalog; the API resolves the authoritative document, verifies pack compatibility, and appends the immutable program plus derived events.
complete_when: A browser can attach only a catalog-published compatible DayProgram reference, and replay remains independent of later catalog changes.

items.title: Scheduled and resolved DayEvent runtime
items.summary: Typed commands, leased scheduler claims, deterministic automatic resolution, host decisions, reward effect application, narrative publication, attention rows, and replayable projections execute DayPrograms through the production transaction boundary.
complete_when: Concurrent scheduler and participant operations converge without duplicate boundaries, rewards, narratives, or projection drift.

items.title: Private DayEvent room lifecycle
items.summary: Private DayEvents derive a stable event channel, grant and revoke membership with participation, transfer access through slot-stable replacement, encrypt private history, and retain read-only history after lock or resolution.
complete_when: Member, withdrawn, replaced, revoked, locked, and non-member role surfaces enforce the same private-room authority across REST, live tickets, media, reconnect, and reload.

items.title: Sixty-player mash acceptance
items.summary: The deterministic local acceptance fixture drives 60 occupied slots, five DayEvents, 300 participant rows, concurrent submissions, two scheduler replicas, public/private narratives, bounded host state, and projection rebuild through production paths.
complete_when: The checked 60-player fixture stays within its contention, query-plan, payload, scheduler, and rebuild regression ceilings.

items.title: Reference-backed private media baseline
items.summary: A command-backed private post reference is checked against the current projection and channel authority at serve time; members receive immutable variant bytes and non-members receive none. Canonical ingest and transcoding are closed by the downstream media capabilities.
complete_when: A command-backed private post serves referenced variant bytes to a member and denies a non-member.

items.title: Canonical private media blob store
items.summary: Bounded local PNG/JPEG ingest applies EXIF orientation, serializes decoder-produced RGBA8 into a versioned canonical record, strips container metadata, derives BLAKE3 identity, and persists it through private fd-relative atomic storage with verified restart lookup; it does not normalize ICC profiles or expose upload, serving, or variants.
complete_when: Malformed and oversized inputs are rejected; metadata is stripped before BLAKE3 identity; equivalent images deduplicate; persistence is atomic and root-confined; restart lookup succeeds.

items.title: AVIF/WebP variant generation
items.summary: A pinned media recipe generates verified thumb, tablet, and full-bounded AVIF/WebP from canonical rasters, commits six private immutable members through a manifest installed last, and reproduces exact bytes across concurrency, restart, and explicit regeneration; this is local recipe proof, not a production codec-quality benchmark.
complete_when: The media core produces validated AVIF/WebP variants for every supported size and can regenerate them from canonical storage.

items.title: Authenticated bounded media upload
items.summary: Server startup now requires a pre-provisioned media root, and an active enabled account can submit bounded raw PNG/JPEG bytes to a prepare-before-persist endpoint that commits one canonical raster plus the fixed six-member variant set and returns only typed immutable handle metadata. Missing, non-account, expired, revoked, disabled, unsupported, mismatched, malformed, dimension-limited, body-limited, and variant-output-limited requests retain no canonical or variant bytes; this is local API/filesystem proof, not post serving, browser, hosted durability, or production upload readiness.
complete_when: Authorized uploads return a persistent handle while malformed, oversized, unsupported, and unauthorized requests fail without retained bytes.

items.title: Uploaded media through a private post
items.summary: An enabled-account player uploads bounded PNG/JPEG bytes, submits only the canonical content id plus alt text, reloads manifest-backed AVIF/WebP from a private post, and a second enabled non-member account receives 403 with a zero-byte body for the exact same URL. This is local scratch-Postgres/filesystem proof, not hosted or object-store durability.
complete_when: A seeded member uploads and posts media, receives the correct variant after reload, and a non-member receives no bytes.

items.title: Mafia private room
items.summary: A real private mafia day-chat room is pack-created, capability-filtered, command-backed, live, reloadable, and denied to non-members.
complete_when: Members can post and recover through the private role URL while non-members never receive room data.

items.title: Role private-message lifecycle
items.summary: The engine declares one slot-stable Role PM per occupied slot; generic private-channel projections and capabilities transfer access on replacement, the incoming account receives private live deltas and durable history/media after reload, and the stale outgoing account receives no thread or media data and cannot append.
complete_when: Role PM creation, membership, posting, receipts, reload, replacement transfer, and stale outgoing denial pass through the real stack.

items.title: Neighborhood, mason, dead, and spectator rooms
items.summary: All supported additional room families are locally complete: pack-declared Mason and Neighbor rooms transfer with stable slots, dead chat follows dead-slot lifecycle authority, and explicit slot-disjoint SpectatorOf grants expose a fixed read-only host-authored room. Each family is encrypted, capability-filtered, live/reload proven, media-authorized, and closed at its stale, non-member, or revoked boundary.
complete_when: Every supported private room family is pack/config-created, encrypted at rest, capability-filtered, replacement-safe, and live/reload proven.

items.title: Account login and account-bound invites
items.summary: Local accounts, opaque sessions, account-bound single-use invites, admin lifecycle controls, and the preserved role-surface adapter are locally proven.
complete_when: A real local account can log in, redeem only its invite, reach the intended role URL, and lose access when disabled or revoked.

items.title: Password storage and rotation security
items.summary: Argon2id storage, authenticated password rotation, session revocation, timing equalization, and bounded credential-attempt state are locally proven.
complete_when: Password verification and rotation preserve equalized failure work, revoke old sessions, and recover after bounded throttling.

items.title: Single-use account recovery
items.summary: Recovery credentials support issue, revoke, consume, expiry, replay rejection, password replacement, and session revocation in the local identity proof.
complete_when: Only one valid recovery credential can replace a password and all invalid, expired, revoked, or replayed credentials fail safely.

items.title: Complete session lifecycle
items.summary: Opaque login, atomic rotation, authenticated logout, password/recovery/disablement invalidation, expiry, and reauthentication preserve the local capability-derived role surfaces and are proven through the scratch-Postgres Chromium identity lane.
complete_when: Login, logout, privilege change, password change, recovery, disablement, expiry, and periodic rotation each enforce the declared session transition.

items.title: Account registration
items.summary: The local registration role URL validates an email-style identifier and password, atomically creates a server-generated unprivileged principal plus opaque session, reaches the seeded game URL in its explicit pending-authority state, and shows duplicate/rate-limit recovery without leaking credentials.
complete_when: A bounded registration route creates an unprivileged account and opaque session, preserves the capability-derived role surface, and rejects duplicate or source-quota attempts with browser-visible recovery.

items.title: Coexisting classic and WorkOS sign-in methods
items.summary: The authentication-method model (principal, methods, one backend-owned app session) is DB-proven end to end: the WorkOS assertion is exchanged once for the same opaque fmss_ session classic uses, a classic method attaches to a WorkOS principal with display-once recovery codes and identical capabilities, removing a method revokes only that method's sessions, the last active method cannot be removed, provider JWTs are rejected as general bearers, and every transition writes identity lifecycle audit rows.
complete_when: One platform principal can authenticate through classic and WorkOS methods interchangeably, convert between them without losing capabilities, and manage methods under recent-authentication, last-active-method, and per-method session-revocation invariants.

items.title: Invite and recovery delivery adapters
items.summary: Invite and recovery issuance seals one-time credentials into redacted typed delivery intents before a lease-claimed provider-neutral outbox worker runs; the scratch-Postgres Chromium lane proves both credential kinds through forced first-attempt failure, declared backoff, provider receipt persistence, GlobalAdmin retry, audit visibility, and the unchanged capability-derived role URL.
complete_when: Invite and recovery delivery are provider-abstracted, retryable, auditable, redacted, and locally testable without claiming live provider traffic.

items.title: Public game index
items.summary: The root board reads a durable public projection of active and completed games, pages by a stable keyset cursor, keeps setup and private lifecycle data out of the query, and is proven through the scratch-Postgres Chromium lane.
complete_when: The public board lists capability-safe active and completed games from a real projection with pagination and browser proof.

items.title: Member data lifecycle and export
items.summary: Authentication can be disabled and game data can be exported, but fmarch does not yet own a coherent member-level deactivation, erasure/pseudonymization, retention, and personal-data export contract.
complete_when: A member can export their associated account data and request a typed lifecycle transition that revokes authority, erases credentials and nonessential identifiers, pseudonymizes retained authorship, and rebuilds every affected projection deterministically under a declared retention policy.
remaining: Define and implement typed member deactivation/erasure facts, deterministic projection pseudonymization, personal-data export, retention boundaries, member controls, and rebuild/browser proof.

items.title: Non-game discussion areas
items.summary: Public non-game discussions use a typed community write model, expected-version appends, enabled-account and profile-backed authorship, independent posting/visibility moderation, canonical topic/post URLs, a public area directory, and a seeded Chromium proof.
complete_when: Users can browse, create, post in, and moderate capability-scoped non-game discussions through real routes and projections.

items.title: User profiles
items.summary: Profiles use durable public and owner-only projections, enabled-account editing, explicit public or members-only visibility, and a seeded Chromium proof.
complete_when: A user can view and edit an authorization-safe profile, with durable projection state and browser proof.

items.title: Public community search
items.summary: A rebuildable PostgreSQL full-text projection searches visible discussions, public profiles, active/completed games, and public main-thread posts with weighted rank, stable cursor pagination, typed filters, excerpts, canonical destinations, and synchronous visibility removal.
complete_when: Users can search public discussions, public game threads, profiles, and games through visibility-safe ranked results with stable pagination and canonical result links.

items.title: Community moderation operations
items.summary: Authenticated members can report public discussion and game-thread posts into typed moderation-case streams with active-report deduplication and bounded daily submissions. GlobalMod operators have a capability-safe queue, reporter evidence, reasoned hide/dismiss/restore transitions, append-only history, and synchronous public-thread/search visibility updates.
complete_when: Members can report public discussion and game-thread content into a durable deduplicated queue, and GlobalMod operators can review, reason, action, restore, and audit those reports through capability-safe routes.

items.title: Community subscriptions and unread inbox
items.summary: Authenticated members can watch public discussion topics and public game threads through one durable member-target stream, receive privacy-safe in-app update references only for active watch periods, and advance a monotonic per-watch read cursor. Fanout is synchronous and rebuildable, author-self updates are excluded, and moderation hide/restore state suppresses and restores inbox entries without mutating history.
complete_when: Authenticated members can subscribe and unsubscribe to public topics and public game threads, receive a durable privacy-safe in-app update inbox, and advance a per-subscription read cursor without polling private audiences or exposing credential principals.

items.title: Personal community mute controls
items.summary: Authenticated members own durable private mute relationships whose read-time overlays suppress public-profile contributions across discussion, search, public game threads, and watched inboxes without changing anyone else's view.
complete_when: Authenticated members can mute and unmute public profiles through a durable private relationship stream, inspect their bounded mute list, and have muted authors consistently suppressed from personalized discussion, search, and inbox reads without changing global visibility or exposing credential principals.

items.title: Portable completed-game export
items.summary: Completed games export a versioned checksum-bearing event manifest through a host role URL; isolated import, projection rebuild, replay audit, and tamper rejection are locally proven.
complete_when: A completed game exports its events, schema/version metadata, referenced projections/media manifest, checksum, and deterministic import/audit result.

items.title: Real hosted identity evidence
items.summary: Local identity code and packet validators are not live hosted account, invite, recovery, abuse-control, session-secret, or retention evidence.
complete_when: A non-fixture redacted operator packet records passed real hosted identity lifecycle and role-surface evidence for every required family.
remaining: Deploy the identity lifecycle and attach real redacted retained/exportable evidence for every hosted family.
blocked_on: Real hosted identity target and operator evidence packet

items.title: Hosted API/frontend deployment evidence
items.summary: Local and hosted-like proof cannot establish an externally reachable deployment or external health checks.
complete_when: Externally reachable API and frontend targets pass the real-hosted preflight and raw-capture contract without fixture or synthetic inputs.
remaining: Provision the hosted target and capture non-synthetic external frontend/API health and flow evidence.
blocked_on: Externally reachable deployment and raw operator capture

items.title: Hosted demo fixtures and sanitized-data policy
items.summary: Local seed fixtures do not prove a hosted demo environment, sanitized data policy, or release-safe invite delivery.
complete_when: The hosted demo target is reproducibly seeded from sanitized policy-approved data and its invite delivery is release-safe.
remaining: Provision and audit hosted demo data, reset policy, and invite delivery.
blocked_on: Hosted demo environment and operator-approved sanitized-data policy

items.title: Production backup and recovery evidence
items.summary: The local backup/restore drill is baseline proof only; it does not establish production storage, PITR, key escrow, or secret rotation.
complete_when: A production-like backup, PITR restore, key escrow, and secret-rotation drill produces retained operator evidence.
remaining: Run and retain the production-like backup/PITR, escrow, and rotation drill.
blocked_on: Production-like storage, keys, secrets, and operator access

items.title: Real hosted concurrent-race evidence
items.summary: The promoted local race matrix does not prove multi-node hosted races, reload/reconnect convergence, or hosted stale-client behavior.
complete_when: The real hosted matrix executes concurrent commands across the deployed topology and records reload, reconnect, and stale-conflict convergence.
remaining: Execute and retain the non-fixture multi-node hosted race matrix.
blocked_on: Stable real hosted topology and external race capture

items.title: Real hosted observability and operations evidence
items.summary: Local structured logs and hosted-like signal bundles do not prove hosted logs, metrics, traces, paging/SLOs, or incident response.
complete_when: The deployed target emits retained logs, metrics, traces, alerts/SLO evidence, and an exercised incident-response receipt.
remaining: Capture real hosted telemetry, alerting/SLO, paging, and incident-response evidence.
blocked_on: Hosted telemetry stack and operator incident-response exercise

items.title: Human beta/release approval
items.summary: No coding agent or generated artifact can approve release ownership, rollback readiness, or support staffing.
complete_when: The release owner reviews product scope and all external evidence, verifies rollback/support staffing, and records explicit approval.
remaining: Obtain and record explicit human release-owner approval after all prerequisites close.
blocked_on: All required product capabilities and operator-owned release evidence

items.title: Record the strict vote-syntax decision
items.summary: Player vote targets are server-supplied controls that emit typed vote commands; the governing docs record that posts are never parsed as votes.
complete_when: The domain and roadmap docs record the shipped strict-target decision and remove the stale open call.

items.title: Ratify the fmarch codename
items.summary: The owner ratified fmarch and the governing architecture, repository, package, domain, and deployment names agree.
complete_when: The owner ratifies the name and the vision/index docs consistently use it.

items.title: Human assistive-technology release review
items.summary: Synthetic interaction checks do not establish that the critical 1.0 journeys work with a real keyboard and screen reader.
complete_when: A retained human keyboard and screen-reader packet covers the critical identity, public, player, host, moderation, inbox, and mute journeys and records successful reruns after every critical fix.
remaining: Run, retain, remediate, and rerun the critical keyboard and screen-reader journey matrix.

items.title: Privacy, terms, retention, and moderation policy approval
items.summary: The codebase does not yet carry owner-approved public policy for data use, retention, acceptable use, moderation, appeals, and support.
complete_when: The operator approves and publishes policy text consistent with the implemented member data lifecycle, retention boundaries, moderation process, appeal route, and support ownership.
remaining: Draft, review, approve, publish, and link the privacy, terms, retention, acceptable-use, moderation-appeal, and support policies.

items.title: Projection snapshots
items.summary: Snapshots are a discardable replay optimization and are excluded from required completion until measured replay cost demands them.
complete_when: A measured replay SLO breach is addressed by versioned discardable snapshots with deterministic fallback to full replay.
remaining: Define a replay benchmark and SLO before deciding whether snapshot implementation is warranted.
items.decision_trigger: Promote only when a representative long-game replay benchmark exceeds the declared latency or resource SLO.

orchestration_rules: The default coding selector may choose only dependency-satisfied incomplete code items; external evidence and human approval never become coding-agent work.
One integrator owns main, central registries, canonical artifacts, commits, and pushes; reviewers remain read-only while a slice is active.
A product-facing capability closes only with its listed acceptance evidence and explicit proof boundary; additional wrappers or commits are not progress by themselves.
Local, fixture, and hosted-like evidence may prepare operator handoffs but cannot complete an external-evidence item.
Optional work remains outside required completion until its decision trigger fires.
